text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: p99 tail-latency spike for customer 'deckline' on hosted inference (region: us-west-2). Alert rule: 'single-tenant tail p99 > 8s'. Triggered at 2026-11-03T10:24:16Z (ts=1766123456).

sre-alex: acked. I'm taking initial triage. Seeing elevated p95/p99 across deckline's dedicated pool.

eng-runtime-maya: grabbing metrics now. Deckline's pool shows p95 ~ 2.4s, p99 ~ 15.8s over last 5m. Streaming chunk stalls and full request stalls both elevated.

ml-oncall-ravi: any unusual prompt shapes? Deckline has a new campaign?

solutions-jane: deckline-ops says they rolled out a large-context prompt template this morning that injects a customer history blob (~4-6k tokens) as prefix for each session.

deckline-ops: confirm. We rolled a personalization prefix to all sessions at 09:50 PT. Users report long waits and occasional 'stalls' where the response stream never resumes. :grimacing:

sre-alex: okay suspected cause: long prefix => KV cache blowouts or sequence-length-dependent kernel fallback. Observed worker restarts correlated with memory pressure on a subset of pods.

eng-runtime-maya: logs (snippet):
```
[2026-11-03T10:21:43Z] worker-34 OOM-kv-cache flush triggered, active_kv_entries=1.2M, seq_max=6144
[2026-11-03T10:22:01Z] worker-41 latency_ms=15800 p99
[2026-11-03T10:22:05Z] runtime: fallback to safe-kernel (slow path) for model: redwood-gptx-13b
```

ml-oncall-ravi: fallback to safe kernels + large KV cache misses would definitely push p99 up. Also possible batching behavior changed: huge prefixes break continuous batching causing many small microbatches -> lower throughput and head-of-line stalls for streaming.

sre-alex: immediate mitigations we can run now: 1) temporarily throttle Deckline quota to reduce concurrent sessions; 2) enable per-tenant prefix caching (if not already) with TTL so identical prefixes hit cache; 3) steer new sessions to a cheaper small-model fallback for Deckline (trade quality for latency). Which can we flip quickly?

eng-runtime-maya: I can flip a routing policy to steer 30% of traffic to 'gptx-13b-lite' (lower memory footprint) in the next 2m. Command:
```
# toggle canary routing for tenant
redwood-cli route update --tenant deckline --policy canary --variant gptx-13b-lite --weight 30
```

sre-alex: do it, and also enable per-tenant rate-limit at 100 rps for now.

eng-runtime-maya: rate-limit command:
```
redwood-cli quota set --tenant deckline --rps 100
```
Applying both now.

incident-bot: action taken summary: routing canary + rate-limit applied (operator: eng-runtime-maya).

deckline-ops: confirm seeing partial improvement — some sessions now return within 2-4s, but heavy sessions still stall. Customers complaining about streaming stalls in long conversations (they see first chunk then silence).

ml-oncall-ravi: follow-up check: are we seeing KV cache thrash? Check kv_cache_hit_rate for tenant.

eng-runtime-maya: kv_cache_hit_rate for deckline dropped from 78% to 19% after the prefix rollout. That's consistent with many unique prefixes.

sre-alex: analysis: new prefix is high-cardinality (user-specific history blob). That will reduce cache hits and increase memory pressure. For a single-tenant dedicated pool this can cause cross-request eviction and disk spill for KV or GC pressure leading to kernel fallback.

pm-omar: what's the customer impact window? We need ETA to restore SLO or to provide rollback guidance.

sre-alex: short-term plan (next 30-90 min):
- Keep rate-limit at 100 rps.
- Keep 30% canary to lite model to reduce pressure.
- Enable prefix dedupe or hash-based shortener on the control plane for Deckline (best-effort) to reduce unique entries.
- Engineering to prepare a rollback of the personalization rollout on Deckline side.

solutions-jane: drafting a message to Deckline support advising them to rollback personalization and offering the canary fallback as a temporary SLO-safe option.

eng-runtime-maya: deploying a quick config: prefix-shortener ON with max_prefix_tokens=1024 for deckline (will drop older tokens beyond limit) — applying now. Command:
```
redwood-cli config set --tenant deckline --prefix-shortener true --max-prefix-tokens 1024
```

incident-bot: config change queued: prefix-shortener toggle by eng-runtime-maya (ts=1766123940).

deckline-ops: can you not drop tokens originally? We need core user history for the product. If dropped, some answers lose context. But we need uptime. Can we do a partial rollback instead?

ml-oncall-ravi: trade-off: partial rollback (disable personalization) will restore latencies faster. Prefix-shortener is a safer alternative while we rework the format to be lower-cardinality (hashed summary). Recommend rollback if they accept temporary loss of personalization.

sre-alex: deckline — ask for business decision. Meanwhile we continue to stabilize infra.

deckline-ops: we'll rollback the personalization immediately across the customer-facing prod (rolled at 09:50). Doing rollback now. ETA 6m.

eng-runtime-maya: noted. I'll keep canary/rate-limit in place until we see p99 back under 6s.

[10:40 UTC] shift-lead: handing off to next on-call (eng-runtime-maya -> sre-alex remains the bridge). Next on-call window picks up at ts=1766124400.

[10:46 UTC] deckline-ops: rollback complete.

eng-runtime-maya: monitoring: p95 down to 1.9s, p99 down to 5.4s after rollback and prefix-shortener. Streaming stall reports dropping.

pm-omar: good. Status: partial mitigated, customer rollback in place, temporary rate-limits + canary still active. Prep post-incident: root cause: high-cardinality prefix causing KV cache thrash -> kernel fallback and memory pressure -> p99 spike and streaming stalls.

sre-alex: action items (owners):
- eng-runtime: add a preflight rule for tenant prefix cardinality (alert when unique-prefix count > threshold) (owner: eng-runtime-maya).
- ml/research: create a recommended prefix encoding pattern for personalization (summarize+hash) (owner: ml-oncall-ravi).
- solutions: update onboarding docs for large-prefix customers with guidance and recommended config flags (owner: solutions-jane).
- support/CS: coordinate rollout/rollback playbook with Deckline (owner: solutions-jane + deckline-ops).

deckline-ops: thanks team. We'll prepare a safer rollout plan and coordinate with your engineering team for an AB test on smaller prefix shards.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared.

sre-alex: marking incident for postmortem. I'll open a postmortem ticket and assign triage to eng-runtime and ML.

eng-runtime-maya: quick note: please capture the exact model kernel fallback traces and worker memstats (I'll attach logs to the ticket). Also let's add a canary that rejects requests > 4096 prefix tokens per tenant by default.

ml-oncall-ravi: agreed. Also we should evaluate if kernel selection heuristics can avoid switching to slow path for certain long-prefix patterns by using a two-pass compilation.

pm-omar: I'll notify account team and coordinate a follow-up meeting with Deckline in 1 business day.

sre-alex: closing thread here — if anything flares, re-open. Thanks all.
